1.1: 1.1 BEDE on Ezra, vol. 2. As Cyrus, the empire of the Chaldeans destroyed, freed the people of God, etc., down to to whom he preaches the faith of his name and the hope of salvation to all who belong to his kingdom, that is, the elect.
1.2: 1.2 And he commanded me to build him a house, etc. BEDE as above. The house or temple of God in the holy Scriptures, etc., down to and likewise in the future await the solemnities of that dedication.
1.3: 1.3 Who is there among you. THE SAME, ibid. Great is the faith of the king in these words, etc., down to and direct their minds and hands to saving works. Let him go up to Jerusalem. THE SAME, ibid. Those who sin or care for worldly things are in the depths: those who desire to please God, let them sigh for heavenly things, let them transcend all the pomps of the world and allurements by love of eternal things, and build a house for God in Judea, in the confession namely of their iniquity and of divine mercy, let them prepare their hearts which God may deign to inhabit and enlighten, and strive to invite their neighbors to the same by words and examples.
1.4: 1.4 And all. BEDE, ibid. The distinction of words is to be noted, etc., down to hence John: We therefore ought to receive such, that we may be fellow helpers of the truth, etc., 3 John 8. Let them help, etc. Those who abound in temporal goods ought not only to minister necessaries to the poor of Christ, but also gladly to work the good things they can for themselves, that by both advantage they may deserve to have a part in the temple of God which is the Church.
1.5: 1.5 And they rose up. BEDE, ibid. Cyrus commanded, nay permitted, all to go up to Jerusalem and build the house of the Lord, etc., down to and therefore deserved to be partaker of the mercy conferred. The chiefs. THE SAME, ibid. It belongs to the chiefs of the fathers, that is of the masters, by work and doctrine to build up the minds of those erring in the study of good work. Scribes learned in the kingdom of heaven, who, carefully examining the merits and senses of the hearers, know how to judge whom they should promote and to what degree of ecclesiastical ministry. That they might go up. THE SAME, ibid. By daily progress as by certain steps he ascends to the height of the virtues which are in the vision of eternal peace. The first steps are to correct one's own life. The second to labor over the errors of neighbors. The highest after good works and doctrine to await the joys of perpetual recompense.
1.6: 1.6 They strengthened their hands with vessels. The companions of the builders' hands, who cannot build, help by giving money when secular persons commit their children or household to preachers to be raised for the Lord, that what they cannot do themselves, through those who can, they may offer to the Lord the gift of their devotion. And with beasts. BEDE, ibid. That is, the slower, etc., down to and as various furniture for building the house of the Lord be given to the chiefs of the fathers. And he brought forth. THE SAME, ibid. The diverse kinds of vessels, etc., down to contains written in the book of eternal memory: in figure of whom it is fittingly subjoined: And he numbered, etc.
1.9: 1.9 And this is. THE SAME, ibid. Because the Lord knows the number of the elect, etc., down to that before they repent they be snatched to perpetual punishment.
2.1: 2.1 These are, etc. Of Judea, namely, not of Babylon. For to this belonged also those born in Babylon of the stock of captives. For with their whole soul they sighed for Judea and Jerusalem, whose figure their leader Zerubbabel bears, who by his very name shows himself born in Babylon, but in intention and work a citizen of Jerusalem. In a higher sense the children of the Church are sons of the heavenly homeland, not only those who are already imbued with the sacraments of the Church, but also those who outside, that is among the impious, sometimes straying, by divine election foreordained before the ages to life, are to be consecrated by the ministries of divine grace. And they returned to Jerusalem. BEDE on Ezra, vol. 2. For when, delivered from the power of Satan, etc., down to the vision of peace and confession is begun in the present, and perfected in the future. Each into his city. THE SAME, ibid. Therefore Scripture watchfully distinguished from what generation of captives they were released and returned to their homeland, etc., down to for whom he will reward with sure recompense.
2.2: 2.2 The number, etc. THE SAME, ibid. He calls the tribe of Judah and Benjamin the people of Israel, etc., down to must be understood together with the priests and Levites who had had a lot among them.
2.58: 2.58 The Nethinim children, etc. THE SAME, ibid. The Nethinim, who are described in order after the priests, Levites, singers, and doorkeepers, were then those who are now called subdeacons in the Church, obedient to the offices of the Levites, and receiving oblations in the temple from the people. All the Nethinim. THE SAME, ibid. In this place also according to the letter the grace of God is shown, by which even in the Old Testament Gentiles were received to salvation, when, the catalogue of those being set forth who were truly known to belong to the people of God, there were added those of whom it was unknown whether they were of Israel or of proselytes: and their number is set forth together among the children of Israel: for though by the long separation of their fathers from the temple or people of God they could not show how they belonged to him, yet, the general license being given, those who had gone up from the captivity were received as associates; for the other Israelites rejoiced to have them from love of common faith and religion as brothers and known, though in origin of flesh they knew them less. Allegorically, however, among the penitents who, freed from the captivity of vices, go up to build the house of the Lord either in themselves or in others, there are some who, bound by very many graver sins, seem to be alienated by God from every act of piety and chastity, so that nothing at all of goodness and religion which they had received from teachers seems to remain in them, nor can they show whether they were born of Israel, that is of holy Church, because such by sinning have become as if they never belonged to the Holy Spirit, yet by repenting they are corrected and converted, that their number may be written among the true Israelites in whom there is no guile, in heaven.
2.61: 2.61 And of the children of the priests. BEDE, ibid. The children of the transmigration act with the same caution toward the priests as toward the people. For they took care that it should be clearly evident who truly belonged to the people of Israel or to the priestly race, who were either suspected or begotten of the sure stock of proselytes, that is strangers. The suspected priests therefore they removed from the office of the altar, until their origin should be made clearer, but none the less they kept them in the company of the migrants with unanimous peace. Mystically, however, the children of the priests going up from the Babylonian captivity seek the writing of their genealogy, and not finding it, are cast out of the priesthood when ministers of the altar fall into such shameful acts or impious doctrines that, even if by repenting they return to the salvation of the soul, yet they are not worthy to be restored to the sacred rank. For though among the faithful they await eternal life, yet they do not find the writing of their rank, which they cannot recover, among the perfect priests. The whole multitude as one man, etc. BEDE, ibid. These signify those who by progress of amended life strive to overcome vices and ascend the height of virtues, but are not yet sufficient for themselves to provide the way of regular life, but are restrained and directed by the industry of those who have gone before in Christ. And in themselves. BEDE, ibid. Mystically, in the temple or people of God are singers, etc., down to and as by the sweetness of their voice help those building the temple.
2.66: 2.66 Their mules. THE SAME, ibid. A mule is begotten of an ass and a mare, a hinny of a horse and a she-ass. Among the men who had gone up from the captivity even the animals by which they were helped are described. And their number is designated like that of men, because there are many in the Church either slower in sense, or even carnal, who yet devoutly obey spiritual masters, and to carry the burdens of fraternal need bow the back of their mind, and with the other elect, rescued from the confusion of the devilish captivity, tend to the walls of the heavenly city, whose number also is kept whole in the memory of God; hence: Your eyes saw my imperfect being, Psalm 138. And elsewhere: Men and beasts you will save, O Lord, ibid. 35.
2.68: 2.68 They offered willingly for the house of God to, etc. THE SAME, ibid. It is a sign of great devotion, etc., down to the more they consider that they do not even use lawful things.
2.69: 2.69 According to their ability. For this is the measure of perfection, that each labor for the Lord according to his power, and confirm the state of the Church first in himself, then in his neighbors. Those who so conduct themselves are rightly called chiefs of the fathers, because in perfection of life and doctrine they rule from a higher place those who in the Church are called fathers by zeal of solicitude. Golden drachmas. BEDE, ibid. Gold and silver and priestly garments, etc., down to For the more gravely they remember they erred, the more ardently they apply themselves to good works.
2.70: 2.70 The priests therefore and Levites dwelt. A Levite captured by the Chaldeans receives a city, when a deacon, by the Lord's gift, restores the virtue of perfection which, seduced by the devil, he had lost. But one born in Babylon enters a city in Judea coming there, when, regenerated in Christ and well instructed in the Church, he regularly keeps the diaconate once received. For as the former by the grace of Christ is as it were delivered from Chaldean servitude, so this one by the execution of the good works in which his predecessors of the same rank lived, ascends as it were to the walls of his own virtue or city. And all Israel. BEDE, as above. All Israel, he does not say only the ten tribes, which were once called Israel to distinguish them from the two which were called Judah, etc., down to of whom the Jews promise themselves, that when their Christ reigns, with the rest of their nation they will return into Judea, and reign over the whole world. Allegorically the priests, Levites, singers, doorkeepers, and Nethinim, and all Israel dwell in their cities, when the ministers of the altar and the teachers and the Christian people serve God faithfully in their ranks, whether those who in the same rank, once stained or lost by vices, have been corrected by repentance, or those who, lately coming from the kingdom of the devil to the Church, have gained for themselves a good rank. For they entered their cities, the Levites or the sons of Israel, not only those who had lost them by being captured, but also those born of captives who had learned that they belonged to them by paternal succession. But whoever were so captured that, never returning, they left their lands to others to possess, signify those who by sinning so depart from the Church that they never come to their senses, and leave to others the rewards promised to them; hence: Be mindful therefore from whence you are fallen, and do penance, and do the first works: or else I come to you, and will move your candlestick, etc., Apocalypse 2; and elsewhere: Hold fast that which you have, that no man take your crown, ibid. 3.
3.1: 3.1 And now the seventh month was come. BEDE on Ezra, vol. 2. Which with us is October, solemn above the others by legal observance, in which also the dedication of the temple was celebrated. Fittingly therefore, when first they had entered their cities and provided dwellings for themselves, soon they flowed together to Jerusalem, and built the altar, and at the time at which the temple with the altar and all vessels was once consecrated, and at which they were wont to come yearly to the day of consecration. Mystically. The seventh month signifies the grace of the Holy Spirit. In this month after the captivity we assemble from our cities in Jerusalem, when, the filth of vices removed, after the beginning of good works we are enlightened by the greater grace of the same Spirit, and are kindled in the love of the heavenly peace, which is in true unity. For Jerusalem is called vision of peace.
3.2: 3.2 And Jeshua arose. Of the priestly tribe, which signifies Christ the true priest, who in his blood washed us from sins, and now stands in the sight of God for us. And his brethren the priests. Of whom it is said: Go, tell my brethren, Matthew 28. These are in the Church the higher, and clinging more familiarly to Christ, build the Church. To the whole Church also it is said: But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood, 1 Peter 2. For the elect are members of the high priest, offering their bodies a living sacrifice. And they built. BEDE, as above. With great forethought they first built the altar, etc., down to but they had not Christ as advocate with the Father.
3.3: 3.3 Its bases. THE SAME, ibid. The hearts, namely, of the elect to receive the sacraments of faith prepared by the precepts of masters as by the iron tools of craftsmen, etc., down to when the faithful submit their hearts and bodies with humble intention to practice by working what they believe. And they offered. BEDE, ibid. Morning and evening we offer a holocaust to the Lord on his altar, etc., down to according to that: Let my prayer be directed as incense in your sight, the lifting up of my hands as evening sacrifice, Psalm 140.
3.4: 3.4 And they kept. THE SAME, ibid. Those who had gone up from Babylon to Jerusalem, etc., down to and elsewhere: We have not here a lasting city, but we seek one to come, Hebrews 13. The feast of tabernacles. Which in Greek is scenopegia, that is the fixing of tabernacles, begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, and lasts seven days: in which the Lord commanded the people to dwell in tabernacles, and daily, searching the law, to offer holocausts to the Lord: because once they dwelt in tabernacles in the wilderness, with the law preached by Moses, and God frequently appearing to them, long awaiting the promised rest, lest ever the grace of so great a benefit should come into oblivion. In order. Because whatever is done without order loses the merit of perfection: because the honor of the king loves judgment. For what we do in honor of the supreme King, we must be sure to distinguish by discretion of judgment when and how much they are to be done.
3.5: 3.5 On the Kalends, as in all, etc. Namely at the beginnings of the months at the rising of the moon, from which the Hebrews always began their months, having no months except lunar: hence for Kalends the Greeks better say neomenias, that is new moons. If, however, the months, because of the thirty days with which they are filled, signify the fullness of the works of light, when in the faith of the holy Trinity we fulfill the precepts of the Decalogue, what do the beginnings of the months, in which the moon, to shine anew, is said to be newly lit by the sun, designate but the beginnings of good working, which, by the grace of the Creator giving, we receive as by the presence of the sun of justice? In significance of which divine illumination, without which we cannot begin or perfect anything good, God commanded all the Kalends, that is the beginnings of the months, to be celebrated; hence: Blow the trumpet at the new moon, on the notable day of your solemnity, Psalm 80. Well it is said, because the feast of tabernacles being finished the children of the transmigration made a perpetual holocaust, etc. Because after the soul has once perfectly renounced this world, it must spend itself wholly in the service of the divine will.
3.6: 3.6 From the first day. From the beginning, namely, of the divine inspiration by which the human conscience is changed, and, pleasures neglected, burns for those things alone which are the Lord's, as the apostles, who inflamed by the Holy Spirit, made as it were a holocaust, preached in all tongues the great works of God. Hence among the Hebrews the seventh month is called the new year: because through the Holy Spirit it is given to the faithful to fulfill the new commandment of charity, and to render a new canticle in the building of the house of God. It is to be noted, however, that in the seventh month the people were gathered in Jerusalem, and, all being assembled, Jeshua and Zerubbabel with his brethren are related to have built the altar, and from the first day of the seventh month to have offered a holocaust: whence it is gathered that this altar was very quickly put together of rough stones: not as in the past made of wood and covered with bronze plates. For otherwise even a very great crowd of workers pressing could not begin and finish in one day, and prepare for offering a holocaust. In the book of the Maccabees it is said to have been made of stones: And they took whole stones according to the law, and built a new altar according to the former, 1 Maccabees 4. It is to be noted that the beginning of the fifth age, like the four preceding, is consecrated by holocausts offered to the Lord. In the first, the protomartyr Abel, first of all the elect, offered to God a holocaust of the firstborn of the sheep, and dedicated the entrance of the nascent world first with the victims of cattle, at length with his own blood. The beginning of the second age Noah consecrated by holocausts offered to God of what had been in the ark. The third age Melchizedek and Abraham hallowed, the one in bread and wine, the other with his own son offered. The fourth age David consecrated to the Lord, building an altar on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, and offering holocausts to God, by which he might appease him whom he had offended by numbering the people; where Abraham is reported to have offered his son, and afterwards, the temple being built by Solomon, the altar of holocausts is established to have been placed. The beginning of the fifth age now Jeshua and Zerubbabel, an altar being built in the same place, and holocausts offered to God, soon, the yoke of captivity shaken off, offered, and afterwards by the perpetual holocaust appeased the Lord for themselves. All these things went before in figure of him who in the sixth age by the victim of his flesh redeemed the whole world.
3.7: 3.7 And they gave. BEDE as above. Those who had come to Jerusalem delivered from captivity, etc., down to The foundation of the temple signifies those who, newly converted, prepare a place for the Lord in themselves; hence: Your members are the temple of the Holy Spirit, etc., 1 Corinthians 6. Masons. THE SAME, ibid. The masons in the construction of the house of God are those who by teaching or rebuking instruct the hearts of neighbors, etc., down to and the tabernacle composed of curtains and boards. Stonecutters. THE SAME, ibid. The stonecutters are the preachers, who, while they join by the bond of charity to one another those whom they train in good works, like squared and polished stones, lest they lose the order of composition, unite them by the pouring in of mortar, saying: Before all things have a constant mutual charity among yourselves, etc., 1 Peter 4. Hence Paul: Above all things have charity, which is the bond of perfection, Colossians 3. To the Sidonians and Tyrians. THE SAME, ibid. The Sidonians also and Tyrians represent preachers, who cast down men once lofty and bright in the glory of the world, secure in the word of God, from the state of their first manner of life, that they may correct them, wholesomely prostrate, and as it were baked out of the corrupting moisture of inborn sense, from all strength of vices, and bring them into adornment or defense of the Church. Hence in the psalm which is inscribed at the consummation of the tabernacle: The voice of the Lord breaking the cedars, Psalm 2. To the Sidonians and Tyrians. BEDE, ibid. The chiefs of the fathers give, etc., down to because they have tribulation in the world, though trusting that the Lord has overcome the world. That they should bring timber. THE SAME, ibid. They bring timber cut in the sea, etc., down to and through the reconciliation of priests we are gathered into the Church. Joppa. Whence, namely, by land they were to be brought for the work of the temple, as was done in the first construction of the temple, but Solomon by royal power easily obtained what he wished from King Hiram: these however returning from captivity and not having the power of a kingdom bought everything. In the year. BEDE as above. Since above it is said that in the seventh month they came to Jerusalem, etc., down to or the resurrection of bodies which we, working well, hope for, he announces.
3.8: 3.8 In Jerusalem. That is, the place of the temple where they desired to build the temple. For the Jews are mistaken who say that the walls of the temple were never overthrown by the Chaldeans, but only the roof, since it is plain that Ezra, the son of the transmigration, made the temple from the foundations. And all who. The great devotion of the whole people. For they rejoiced that they had returned from captivity, and as much as they shuddered at the crimes of the proud city, so much did they long to see the beauty of Jerusalem: as much as they abominated the shrines of idols, so much did they strive to have the temple of God restored. So not only bishops and priests ought to build up the people of the faithful, that is the house of God, but also the people, called from the captivity of vices to the vision of true peace, ought to choose the ministry of the word from those who know how to teach, namely the ministers of the word, that is the Levites, who are appointed from twenty years and upward: because such are appointed to preach and are to be preferred as show the Decalogue to their hearers not only by doing it, but also keep the purity and integrity of the heart unspotted in the sight of God. From twenty years. BEDE as above. There is no doubt that here the state of the Church takes its projected course through the Spirit, etc., down to but Zerubbabel sprang from the royal tribe.
3.9: 3.9 And there stood. THE SAME, ibid. Not the son of Jozadak, etc., down to They praise also by the hand of David the king, when they diligently attend to and imitate, as far as they can, the works of Christ which he did in the flesh.
3.10: 3.10 The priests stood in their apparel. THE SAME, ibid. The great devotion of all persons is shown, when, the temple being founded, all according to their rank praise the mercy of the Lord. The priests, adorned in holy vestments as they had been accustomed while the temple still stood, sounding with trumpets and kindling the heart of the people to the sweetness of heavenly praise; the Levites with well-sounding cymbals singing hymns to the Lord; the people showing the affection of the heart by a common shout in praising God.
3.11: 3.11 And they sang together in hymns. That is, on the instruments which he himself made, or the psalms which he appointed, or because David, at the placing of the ark, made Asaph chief to confess to the Lord, with his brethren, as Chronicles testifies, of whom again it is said: For his sons were under his hand prophesying beside the king, 1 Chronicles 15, 16. Rightly, when the sons of Asaph praised and confessed to the Lord by the hand of David, they are to be understood to have done this according to his arrangement.
3.12: 3.12 They wept. BEDE as above, seeing namely how far the poverty of that time fell short of the once magnificent power of Solomon, by which the first temple was founded, etc., down to In the second Christ and the apostles announce the grace of the New Testament and the entrance of the heavenly kingdom. THE SAME, ibid. They wept at the building of the spiritual temple, etc., down to nor among the increases of the pious are the trials of the wicked lacking, who, either by feigning good or openly bringing in evil, strive to hurt the saints.
4.1: 4.1 Now the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard, etc. BEDE on Ezra. By the enemies of Judah and Benjamin he means the Samaritans, etc., down to who are about to receive at the right hand of the judge the blessing and the eternal kingdom. They say therefore:
4.2: 4.2 Let us build with you. THE SAME, ibid. When heretics seek to be granted the authority of preaching among Catholics, etc., down to he attacked most fiercely in the person of an open enemy. It is not for us. It is not for heretics to build the Church, from which they are estranged, but only for those who, adhering to Christ the true king and priest, have deserved to be called chiefs of the fathers, and for the pious care which they have for those who desire to see Christ.
4.3: 4.3 But. THE SAME, ibid. As often as heretics, not only in the cities but also in the provinces, by teaching perversely or even by raging, hindered the doctrine of the true confession, etc., down to there would be abundance for the wise master builders to rebuild the same house after the captivity.
4.4: 4.4 The people of Judah. By the people of Judah, that is confessing and glorifying, he means him who seeks to build wholly for the Lord, that is to turn the minds and mouths of all he can to doing his will and seeking his glory.
4.5: 4.5 They hired. THE SAME, ibid. The distinction of the words is to be noted, etc., down to when they obtain the protection of earthly princes against the Church, how much this harms the faith became clearer than light in the time of Arian perfidy. And in the reign of Ahasuerus. THE SAME, ibid. This Artaxerxes, etc., down to but permitted him, as of lesser power, to deal with and decide these things. BEDE, ibid. Artaxerxes, who is persuaded and, persuaded, commanded that Jerusalem not be built, etc., down to the enemies who held the neighboring places having again been overcome, they possessed them.
4.14: 4.14 Injuries. Because those who try to assail the kingdom of the devil cannot bear them, they fear wars stirred up in the Church, lest their heresies and falsehoods be conquered together with the doctrine of the Gentiles, under the leadership of him who says: I came not to send peace, but the sword, Matthew 16. And again: I am come to cast fire on the earth, Luke 12., etc., the sword namely of the word of God, with which he lays low his adversaries, the fire of charity, by which, kindling the hearts of his own, he burns up all the arms and shields of the opposing sect. For the city. BEDE as above. The enemies themselves again confess concerning the city of the Lord, etc., down to that is, the beginning and perfection of honors they render to God, from whom they received them, by living well and giving thanks.
4.16: 4.16 Beyond the river. The Euphrates, namely, within which Syria lies, which signifies baptism, because it is one of the four rivers of paradise which water the whole world, just as the four evangelists, inspired from one fountain of life, that is Christ, preach with harmonious voice to all nations the laver of salvation; or because Euphrates is interpreted fruitful: which fits the sacrament by which the world, washed and sanctified, brings forth to God the fruit of souls, thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold.
4.17: 4.17 The king sent a word to Rehum the chancellor. BEDE as above. The king of the Persians inquires, etc., down to who persecute the Church and forbid it to be built. The inhabitants of Samaria. The enemies of Jerusalem dwell in Samaria, which is interpreted keeping, not that they who obstinately oppose the vision of true peace keep the precepts of faith and truth, but because they boast that the keeping of virtues remains with themselves, while through heresy they fight against the walls of peace.
4.23: 4.23 So the copy. BEDE, ibid. The order of the history is plain, etc., down to and the king had only forbidden the city to be built.
5.1: 5.1 Prophesied. BEDE, book II on Ezra, vol. 2. In their books it is written more fully, etc., down to Zerubbabel also and Jeshua, and the people who were with them, are proved to have been of no less faith, who rather heeded the prophets who commanded than the command of him who forbade.
5.2: 5.2 Zerubbabel. THE SAME, ibid. Born in Babylon, etc., down to Everyone also, when calling upon God, seeks nothing else than himself, can call him Shealtiel. And Jeshua. THE SAME, ibid. Joshua or Jesus is interpreted Savior. Jozadak, the just Lord. He indeed, like the son of Nun, signifies Christ; for each led a people into the promised land, the one from the long sojourn of the desert, the other from the longer servitude of captivity. So the true Jesus, rescuing his elect from all evils, leads them in to the promised joys of the heavenly kingdom, who is the son of Jozadak, that is of the just Lord, of whom it is said: The just Lord will cut the necks of sinners, etc., Psalm 128.
5.3: 5.3 At the same time. THE SAME, ibid. The letter of the text is plain, that, strengthened by the words of the prophets, the nobles of the Jews could not be hindered from the holy work by the attacks of enemies, from which, while the prophets were still silent, they had ceased through fear of the enemies, just as it is now done in the Church, when those who, held back by the snares of malignant spirits or men, were sometimes slower to the good work, suddenly rebuked by the words of teachers or of the divine Scriptures, can be conquered by no devices of temptations, nor recalled from the purpose of their intention.
5.4: 5.4 To which we answered. THE SAME, ibid. It seems that he who wrote this was present, though Ezra is said to have written it, who is found not to have been at Jerusalem then, but to have come there much later, in the reign of Artaxerxes. Either then he was truly there at that time, and, the temple being made, returned to Babylon, to bring back more of the children of Israel to Jerusalem, or he joins himself to the builders, as if what is done among his brethren, or what they themselves do, were his own, as the Apostle says: We who are alive, who remain unto the coming of the Lord, shall not prevent, etc., 1 Thessalonians 4.
5.6: 5.6 The copy of the letter. THE SAME, ibid. This letter is very unlike that one, etc., down to and at last, knowing that this had its origin from the God of heaven and earth, who alone is truly God, they take part in his sacrifices and rejoice to help the building.
5.8: 5.8 With unpolished stone. THE SAME, ibid. A new one, namely, which they found unpolished, but by polishing fitted to the building, etc., down to another, given over to idolatry, with no industry of spiritual architects, with no worship of piety had put off the deformity of a rustic and earthly mind. And timber is laid in the walls, and the work, etc. THE SAME, ibid. The timbers, which are placed for the ornament or defense of the temple, designate the same life of the saints in the adornment of the Church that the stones do: of which it is said: All the trees of the woods shall rejoice, etc.
6.1: 6.1 Then Darius. BEDE on Ezra, book 2, vol. 2. Josephus gave the name of the place in which this letter of Cyrus was found thus: and a book was found in Ecbatana, a city built in the region of Media. Another translation, however, has it thus: In Ecbatana in the most secure building of the region of the Medes: whence it appears that the name Medena signifies nothing other than Media.
6.3: 6.3 That they lay the foundations. THE SAME, ibid. We need not expound, etc., down to or of the porch of the house of the Lord which were before the face of the temple. Of which Scripture, when the palace of Solomon was being built, speaks thus: He made the court, etc., 3 Kings 7.
6.5: 6.5 Let them be restored. THE SAME, ibid. Darius confirms the finished letters by his authority, restraining all the adversaries of the Jews, and commands the temple to be built in its place, etc.
6.6: 6.6 Now therefore. Artaxerxes, who forbids the house of God and the city to be built, signifies those who, by stirring up persecutions, oppose the building of the holy Church, among which persecutions the Church flourished most by the victory of the martyrs. Darius, however, signifies the pious devotion of those kings who, having recognized the piety of the Christian faith, took care not to resist it but to help it by their decrees, many of whom, the persecutions of their predecessors forbidden, wished themselves with their subject peoples to be consecrated by the sacraments of the same faith: to whom well agrees what Darius adds: But by me the command is given, etc. For who could explain how much the Church has been helped and enriched by the liberality of kings?
6.8: 6.8 That from the treasury. BEDE, ibid. From the king's treasury expenses are granted for the work of God, etc., down to what Cyril, what John, what the other saints said: he proved he was taught by the elders of the Jews, that is, of those confessing and praising God. Calves and lambs. THE SAME, ibid. These animals, which are clean, etc., down to whatever wholesome thing he has learned from the men of the Church, he spends it all on divine worship.
6.9: 6.9 According to the rite. For the vows of the offerers will be acceptable only when they are offered according to the rite of Catholic peace; but those mixed with Gentile superstition or heresy are not good.
6.10: 6.10 And let them pray. According to that of the Apostle: I desire therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all men, for kings, and for all that are in high station, 1 Timothy 2.
6.11: 6.11 By me therefore. He wished to punish with the gravest penalty him who should change the decree, namely with the loss of all he had and of his own life, which he would lose, fixed to a beam in long torment. Mystically, however, our works are compared to timbers, the good to fruit-bearing ones, the evil to willows and worthy of the fire; and a beam is taken from the house of him who opposes the holocausts of the Lord, and is set up, and he himself is fixed upon it, when the works of those who oppose the peace of the Church are made manifest to all, how useless and perverse they are: and they themselves are proved to have gained in them not the joy of life but the snare of death. The house also of such men is confiscated, that is, proscribed by public census: when the bodies with which they remained in this life are handed over in the resurrection, to be punished with perpetual torment, to cruel exactors, the unclean spirits, into their power.
6.12: 6.12 And God. He desires his decree to be confirmed by the divine power, and he himself, as a man endowed with a temporal kingdom, does by public law all he can for the peace of the house of God. Which is now also done in the Church, when earthly powers converted to the faith issue public edicts for the state of the Church, and she, the Lord helping and conquering her enemies, begins always to have calm peace.
6.14: 6.14 According to the prophecy. For they had foretold that if they persevered in building the temple, soon, the Lord giving, they would complete the work itself and abound in all good things. BEDE as above. No one who says that Haggai says the foundations of the temple were laid under King Darius, etc., down to sometimes separately under the name of treasuries, or exedrae, or porches, or courts; whence: You that stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God, Psalm 133. And Artaxerxes. It is asked how, at the command of Artaxerxes, the house is said to be built, when it is immediately added that it was completed and dedicated while Darius still reigned, unless perhaps we must believe that Artaxerxes also, sending gold and silver, commanded that if anything were less complete in the building or ornament of the temple or the vessels, it should be perfected. For when Ezra was hastening there, it is written that the same king with his princes or counselors sent very much gold and silver and vessels to the temple.
6.15: 6.15 The month of Adar. BEDE, ibid. On the third day of which the house was completed, etc., down to in which all the more eminent things were completed. THE SAME, ibid. The temple, although it signifies the elect soul on account of the Spirit of Christ dwelling in it, etc., down to and from the higher we penetrate also to the third, when we heap up the blessedness of souls with the reception of immortal bodies.
6.16: 6.16 And the children. Rightly do the children of the transmigration rejoice, etc., down to because all the ranks of the Church rejoice over sinners reconciled by penance.
6.17: 6.17 And they offered. At the dedication they offer victims, when they give thanks to God for the conversion of the erring, when many, seeing their devotion, gird themselves to greater works of virtue, lest they be slower than they in working, to whom they were more innocent by sinning less. Many also who went before in the faith emulate the more fervent zeal of the newcomers. He-goats of the goats. He-goats are offered in this life for sin, when the elect beseech God to be freed from sins: they are offered in the future, when those who have been freed give thanks, and therefore they shall sing the mercies of the Lord forever, Psalm 88.; because they will always remember that they were wretched and have been freed by his gift. For sin. They offer also for the sin of all Israel, because it is fitting that thus we favor the goods of those who are with us, so by imitating their goods we make them ours, that we may also entreat the Lord for the state of the whole Church. Hence in the Lord's Prayer no one asks anything specially for himself, but for all who have the same Father in heaven. Likewise, the temple being built, the dedication follows, when the fullness of the elect completed at the end of the age shall come to the grace of the heavenly rewards, in which victims are offered: of which the same house, that is the Church, rebuilt after the captivity of mortal misery through the glory of immortality, says: You have broken my bonds, O Lord, I will sacrifice to you the sacrifice of praise, Psalm 115. And because they are offered not only for the gifts of virtues, but also for the worldly filth of vices, well after calves, rams and lambs are he-goats offered for the sin of all Israel: for the grace from which it confers the benefits of virtues also takes away crimes. Nor has Pelagius a place in the house of God, who persuaded himself and his followers that by freedom of the will they could either be freed from evils or be confirmed in goods.
6.18: 6.18 And they set. Order demanded that, the house of God being built, priests and Levites to minister in it should soon be ordained. Which is to be observed by those who build monasteries magnificently, that they appoint in them teachers who exhort the people to the works of God, not serve their own pleasures there. Priests. BEDE as above. That he says priests in their orders, etc., down to if we take care to come with them to the rewards of the Lord.
6.19: 6.19 And the children. Therefore, the house of the Lord having been built and dedicated, the celebration of the Passover is specially mentioned, though it was doubtful to no one that the religious then kept the Passover in its time, in order that it might be mystically hinted that this is the summit of perfection, when, all the enticements of the world past, we meditate with the whole intention of the mind on the entrance of another life. For Passover is interpreted passage, because the children of Israel in it, by the immolation of the lamb, passed from Egyptian servitude to freedom, or the Lamb himself, that is Christ, immolated for us, passed from this world to the Father, which we imitate when we pass from lowest pleasures to seek heavenly things, and truly accomplish it when, freed from the prison of the flesh, we enter the heavenly kingdom. BEDE, ibid. Why the Passover is related after the house was built, etc., down to the longer it held the land of the heart empty of virtue.
6.22: 6.22 And they kept the solemnity. THE SAME, ibid. In this place the celebration of the Passover can be typically referred to the time of our resurrection, etc., down to whose sevenfold grace the Prophet commends to us. Seven days. Because through all the time of the age, life is to be led in sincerity and truth, indeed in all the victims and holocausts of the good: because Christ at the Paschal time tasted death for a while, but overcame it by the eternal power of the resurrection. In joy. For this is the greatest joy of the just now and in the future, that the work of justice, or of the Church, is perfect, the Gentiles also, who once resisted, being converted, and to help her state, to confirm the peace of the Christian religion throughout the world.
7.1: 7.1 After these things. Bede on Ezra, vol. 2. Thus far the return of the people from Babylon to Jerusalem, etc., down to they might have whence, admonished, they might learn inwardly to be restored, whence follows: After these things. BEDE, ibid. This Artaxerxes, under whom Ezra went up from Babylonia to Jerusalem, Josephus thinks to be Xerxes the son of Darius, who reigned after him: but the books of the chronicles say the successor of that same Xerxes. Darius, however, under whom the temple was built, reigned thirty-six years, after him Xerxes twenty years, after him Artabanus seven months, which the chronographers counted as a year: after him Artaxerxes forty years. THE SAME, ibid. Ezra is called a ready scribe in the law of Moses, etc., down to the earlier letters remained with the Samaritans, with which they were accustomed to write those five books of Moses, which alone they had received of holy Scripture.
7.7: 7.7 And there went up. THE SAME, ibid. It is to be noted that at the head of this book it is written that by the permission of Cyrus Zerubbabel and Jeshua went up from Babylon, etc., down to to those arriving at the heavenly homeland perpetually I give.
7.9: 7.9 For on the first. THE SAME, ibid. On the first day of the month he began to go up from Babylon, etc., down to as if after four months of bright action, which we spend on the way, we spend the fifth month of perpetual reward in the light of the heavenly homeland. THE SAME, ibid. In the first month Ezra began to go up from Babylon, etc., down to we may come to the heavenly promises. According to the hand of God. Strengthened, namely, by divine grace and protection, by which he might perfect what was prosperously begun. So Christ also, because God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, the hand of God was also upon his humanity, by which, exalted in the passion, he ascended to the walls of the heavenly city and opened the way for his faithful.
7.10: 7.10 For Ezra prepared. It is a great virtue in a man to prepare his heart for obedience to the divine will, and to be able to say: My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready, Psalm 56. BEDE, ibid. Christ also prepared his heart to search the law of the Lord, because he foresaw that God would take to himself such a man as would be not only without sin, but full of grace and truth: who, with no law of sin resisting him, kept the law of God without any contradiction of mind or flesh; hence: In the head of the book it is written of me, etc., Psalm 39. Likewise the Lord searched the law of God, because, casting aside the traditions of the Pharisees, he taught that holy Scripture is to be understood mystically, and showed the decrees of the Gospel which he brought to be more perfect and acceptable to God than those he had premised through Moses. Hence: You have heard that it was said to them of old: You shall love your friend, and hate your enemy. But I say to you: Love your enemies, etc.
7.12: 7.12 Artaxerxes the king. Artaxerxes, who with a devout mind venerated the temple and priests of the Lord and served him, signifies Christian princes, as Darius does. Nor is it wonderful if the successors of Cyrus, who had the temple and city built, who loved and helped his servants and the law, figure Christian kings; since the Lord himself said by the prophet that Cyrus signifies his Son, and honored him by his name, saying: Thus says the Lord to my Christ Cyrus, Isaiah 45.
7.13: 7.13 By me a decree. Because the fame of the divine power had reached the king, through which he renewed the law burnt by the Chaldeans in the same words as before, though in another character of letters.
7.14: 7.14 That whoever. He grants to all permission to go, compels no one to go. Christian princes, compelling no one, lest the will of faith be uncertain, permit all who please to worship Christ in their kingdom. And of his seven counselors. In the book of Esther it is read that it was the custom of the kings of the Persians, in all things to be done or decided, to use the counsel of seven. The faithful use seven counselors when in all that they do they follow the precepts of divine Scripture. Of which it is said: The words of the Lord are pure words, as silver tried by the fire, purged from the earth, refined seven times, Psalm 11., that is made perfect by the holy illumination of the sevenfold spirit. You are sent. Ezra is sent from the face of the king and his seven counselors to visit India and Jerusalem, and the princes of the age converted to the faith and strengthened by the persuasions of the Scriptures desire Christ to come to save the Church and gather it from the nations with daily help, which the name of Ezra signifies, saying: O Lord God of hosts, turn, look from heaven, etc., Psalm 79. Which is in the hand. It is wonderful that a word is found in the letter of Artaxerxes which the prophets are accustomed to use: when he says the law of God is in the hand of his servant; for it is written: The word came in the hand of Haggai the prophet. And the Lord did what he spoke in the hand of his servant Elijah; and the Lord testified in Israel and in Judah by the hands of all the prophets: because the prophets preached the things of God no less by doing than by speaking. Christ had the law in his hand: because he once established it through Moses as he willed; and now, changing it by himself, he has brought it to more perfect things.
7.15: 7.15 And that you bear. The faith and wisdom of the king and his counselors are to be noted, who understood that their gifts should rather be offered through him who had the law of God in his hand, that is, fulfilled it in work. Whose in Jerusalem. BEDE as above. He says faithfully and learnedly that he has his tabernacle in Jerusalem, etc., down to and of him John says: He is the propitiation for our sins, 1 John 2.
7.16: 7.16 And all the silver. By this money the faithful in his Church desire their good works to shine: that through this they may have the Father with the saints: and others may profit by their examples. For as from our silver and gold, sacrifices, libations and victims are provided to offer to the Lord: when, seeing the brightness of our works, our neighbors are converted to the duty of piety: by which they too, living well, are consecrated to the Lord; there are, however, some most shining virtues of the saints which cannot be shown to all as examples of work: but only recited to glorify the grace of God, such as that which Daniel and Jeremiah as boys prophesied: that John not yet born: that Cornelius with his house, not yet baptized, received the Holy Spirit, and countless miracles, like silver, in the house of the Lord. Nor can the offerings which are placed upon the altar be bought only from this silver or gold, because when we hear such things we ought indeed to wonder at them as divine: but as possible we are not able to imitate them.
7.19: 7.19 The vessels also. The true Ezra delivered into the heavenly Jerusalem, in the sight of the Father, the vessels of mercy which are handed over to him by men. Of which it is said: How can anyone enter into the house of the strong and spoil his goods, unless he first bind the strong? Mark 3. For the strong one was the king of Babylon, that is the devil: but bound and fettered by the Lord, he lost the vessels which he unjustly possessed, that is the hearts of the elect: nor could he gainsay him who took them away and brought them back to the heavenly city to which they belonged.
7.21: 7.21 And by me. Christian princes command their subjects to give without delay whatever Christ our high priest asks, retracting nothing at all: let them give gold in the confession of the true faith, wheat in the showing of good works; wine in the fervor of love; oil in the cheerfulness of mercy: and all these things are commanded to be given by the hundred to the great priest and scribe of the law of the God of heaven, that is to Christ, who, bringing us from the Father the heavenly commandments, promised heavenly rewards to the obedient in the house of the Father. For the hundred, which in the reckoning of the fingers passes from the left to the right hand, designates the things on the right, in the index, that is the joys of eternal life. A talent, however, is handed down in a threefold measure. The least, of fifty pounds, the middle, of sixty-two pounds, the greatest, of a hundred and twenty pounds. A cor is thirty measures: a bath, which is also the tenth part of an ephah, a cor, is three measures.
7.22: 7.22 And salt. BEDE as above. Salt signifies wisdom, etc., down to while they fight them through their adversaries.
7.24: 7.24 To you also. By this privilege it is shown that the rest of the people of the children of Israel, coming to their homeland, paid the king's tribute, which the king is known to have done by discriminating provision, that those who were occupied in the divine service should be free from his service, and that those who possessed nothing of their own on earth but lived from the tithes of the people should have no tribute exacted from them by anyone. By all these things he is proved not only to have loved, but also to have learned most thoroughly what the worship of divine service requires.
7.25: 7.25 But you. BEDE, ibid. The king repeats what he had said above, etc., down to to whom kings and princes often sent letters for the state of the faithful.
7.28: 7.28 And I was strengthened. So each is made fit by his teaching to gather others: strengthened by the grace of God, he is made strong in mind against all things that hinder the work of the saints.
8.1: 8.1 These are therefore the chiefs, etc. BEDE, on Ezra. He diligently enumerates the chiefs who went up with him from Babylon, etc., down to that is, from the life of those whom you have taught, you will be more glorious in the kingdom of God.
8.15: 8.15 And I gathered. BEDE, ibid. I do not remember reading this name of the place elsewhere, etc., down to he provided for himself a supply of ministers of the house of God, through whom, coming to Jerusalem, he might perform what was necessary for the uses of the temple.
8.17: 8.17 And I sent them to Iddo. THE SAME, ibid. The Caspian Sea according to Orosius, etc., down to to whom added, Ezra is found to have had in his company a sum of nearly seventeen hundred men.
8.21: 8.21 And I proclaimed there a fast. BEDE, hom. 8. An example is given us of fasting and praying, etc., down to and so let him pray, nor doubt that what he asks will come about prosperously.
8.25: 8.25 And I weighed to them the silver, and the gold, and the consecrated vessels. THE SAME on Ezra, vol. 2. By the silver, and gold, and vessels which are sent from Babylon to Jerusalem, etc., down to and through their successors is to be built until the end. THE SAME, ibid. There is a difference between these vessels which Ezra with the priests offers at Jerusalem and those which Zerubbabel and Jeshua are related to have offered: because those were carried from the temple of the Lord into Babylon, and were carried back into Jerusalem: these were made in Babylonia, but sent to Jerusalem out of devotion by the king or princes of the Persians, or even by the people of Israel who dwelt in those parts. Those vessels, then, signify those who, after receiving the knowledge and sacraments of the faith, after beginning the works of virtue, deceived by the devil, are snatched into their confusion, but by the grace of Christ are recalled to salvation: these, however, signify those who, born with the sin of the first transgression, cleansed by the laver of regeneration through the ministry of priests, are gathered to the children of the Church.
8.28: 8.28 You are holy to the Lord. The teachers of the Church ought never to forget holiness, because they are consecrated by the Lord through the Holy Spirit unto the day of redemption, to receive which they should also instruct their hearers, that those who have already been offered to the Lord through the rudiments of the faith may be still more confirmed by the examples and admonitions of those who went before in the faith, and be made worthy of entrance into the heavenly city.
8.29: 8.29 Watch and keep. Priests must watch lest any of the souls entrusted to them, that is of the vessels of the Lord, perish: but that they be led in full number to the buildings of holy virtue. Until you weigh them. That is, those whom the heavenly disposition has committed to you, you may present, by instructing and teaching, such as may be found blameless and fit for the treasure of the heavenly hall, that is, for the seats of eternal peace and light, and this not by the judgment of any men whatever who can be deceived, but of the apostles and of those who will judge with the Lord. These are rightly the chiefs of the priests and Levites and the leaders of the families of Israel, that is they are understood to be men or souls seeing God, of whom it is said: You shall make them princes over all the earth, Psalm 44.; and elsewhere: Her husband is honorable in the gates. We have moved. BEDE, ibid. All things are full of mysteries, etc., down to helped by which we may more effectively transfer the souls of the faithful to the fellowship of the elect and the citadel of the perfection of life, as holy vessels to the temple of the Lord.
8.32: 8.32 And we abode. THE SAME, ibid. They abide three days in Jerusalem, etc., down to as if after the joy of the three days' stay in Jerusalem, for the gifts and precious vessels which they offered, they are more honored.
8.34: 8.34 And all was numbered. THE SAME, ibid. This is done when teachers diligently examine the life of their subjects, etc., down to that he may be given a worthy reward in heaven.
8.35: 8.35 But also they that were come. THE SAME. Great devotion and religion are shown when those who arrive at the temple first of all offer holocausts, not only for themselves, but also for all Israel, that is for those who had already returned home and for those who were still in exile. Mystically, however, those truly and perfectly escape by penance the captivity of the devil, in which they were held by sinning, who with fixed intention subject themselves to the divine service, who, drawn away wholly from lowly things, kindle themselves with the flame of heavenly desire. For this is to offer holocausts, that is, wholly burnt sacrifices to the Lord, to think or do nothing in all things except his will. They offered holocausts to God, etc. Not only for themselves. It is the mark of a perfect mind when one immolates for all Israel, that is for the general welfare of the faithful, as if mindful of unity and brotherhood he supplicates the heavenly mercy.
8.36: 8.36 And they lifted up the people. AUGUSTINE. By adorning with various gifts which the king and counselors and his princes had sent, and by freeing also his ministers and priests from all distresses. Mystically. The people and the temple of God hold one and the same figure of the Church, which Ezra and the children of the transmigration lift up, the sacred vessels having been carried out of Babylon, when the preachers, gathering to it by the Lord's help new peoples of believers, render it honorable and terrible to all. Likewise when they advance or promote those whom they have instructed by examples in good conduct or by words up to the reception of the heavenly rewards: they lift up the people into the house of God, because they make great joy both for those who dwell in the heavenly homeland and for the elect who are still pilgrims on earth. BEDE on Ezra, book 2, vol. 2. This transgression, plainly described in the prophet Malachi, etc., down to they refer the case to the prince, that is, the archbishop, by whose authority the crime is to be expiated. All the sins also by which the heathen are polluted, while Christians are not ashamed to imitate them, as if through foreign wives degenerate from the seed of the word of God, by which they had been begotten, according to that: Of his own will he has begotten us by the word, etc., James 1., and as if they beget a profane offspring of the daughters of strangers, while, following the allurements of the erring, they bring their perverse deeds from them to the notice of all. He is not separated. BEDE, ibid. It is to be noted that when Israel was led away into captivity, etc., down to the princes who ought to have corrected confess that they were the first to err.
9.3: 9.3 I rent my cloak. THE SAME, ibid. By garments works are wont to be designated, etc., down to He sat mourning, that by the laments of penance he might teach that pardon is to be deserved.
9.4: 9.4 Assembled. Note how much the examples of teachers help. Nothing is written of Ezra having spoken, but only that, having heard of the crime, he wept, and drew a crowd of the faithful to himself not by shouting but by weeping. Assembled. A great change of things from the perfidy of the princes: many who had followed luxury were brought back, a great prince mourning and hinting what was to be done by sinners: all who fear the word of God, by which he threatens that transgressors are to be punished, assemble to him. The cloak being rent. BEDE, ibid. Typically, that the garment being rent, etc., down to even those things which truly suited their frailty, he mercifully deigned to take upon himself.
9.5: 9.5 I bowed my knees, etc. He prepared himself by compunction of heart and affliction of body, that he might be made worthy to hear the heavenly mercy: and he bursts into these words of prayer. He bends the knees, spreads out his hands, and pours out prayers at the time of the evening sacrifice, knowing that what is done in a spirit of humility and a contrite heart is more pleasing than what is offered of the flesh and blood of cattle.
10.1: 10.1 So while Ezra prayed, and besought God, and wept... The people wept. BEDE on Ezra, vol. 2. Those namely who had sinned, doing penance, or who had remained in chastity, grieving at the fall of their brethren, etc., down to But now even those who sinned, with their wives and children, came together to do penance. Of the sons of Elam. Josephus says this man was the first of the Jerusalemites, who, as befits a prince, with the greatest authority soon helped Ezra's intention, confessing that the people had sinned with him, and urging penance, the foreign wives being cast off with their children. And now if there is penance in Israel. Because if the people repent perfectly of this sin, first converted to the Lord, let us promise correction and ask pardon; then, returned to ourselves, let us root out every root and shoot of sin, casting out, namely, the wives with all their offspring: for this is truly to do penance with the whole heart, and to be turned to the Lord within, and to cut off from its very origin all outward matter of sinning. Arise. He fittingly teaches how matters are to be handled in counsel among elders, namely that each, according to his own judgment, say what he has understood, or seems to himself to have understood, to be best: and yet leave to him who presides the place of deciding, ready to obey all that he, according to the will and law of God, decrees to be done.
10.6: 10.6 The sons of Eliashib. Who was then the high priest: after Jeshua the son of Jozadak, Joiakim his son, and after him Eliashib his son held the high priesthood. He ate no bread. BEDE as above. Priests have an example here, etc., down to: For if, flying from the pollutions of the world, etc., 2 Peter 2.
10.9: 10.9 It was. BEDE as above. Which is called Chislev by the Hebrews, by the Romans December, etc., down to by which art they may either avoid or separate the adversities which rage outwardly on account of sins. And all the people sat. THE SAME, ibid. That is, around the court of the priests, by which the house itself was surrounded on all sides, having around it on every side in a square the very ample buildings of the courts, in which also the people, when there was need on account of rain, could stand and see what was done at the gates of the temple, or around the temple: for they had the inner walls near the ground made on pillars, the outer ones solid.
10.10: 10.10 And Ezra arose. THE SAME, ibid. This place corresponds, etc., down to and rightly be kept in memory, and be handed down to posterity to be known.
10.16: 10.16 And they sat down on the day. THE SAME, ibid. Note that the number three is mystical, etc., down to which we also ought to imitate every year in the Lent of Easter, namely, when the Lord's resurrection is at hand, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, that we may be able to be partakers of the resurrection, 2 Corinthians 7. And there were found. THE SAME, ibid. The Hebrews adapt to this place, etc., down to But it must be observed that Ezra does not write that Jeshua took a foreign wife, but certain of his sons and brethren, etc.

His kinsmen, namely, for his brothers german in the flesh could not still be living and giving themselves to pleasure, when a hundred years and more had passed since Cyrus, beginning to reign, sent back Jeshua and Zerubbabel with the transmigration of Judah and Benjamin to Jerusalem to build the house of the Lord.
10.19: 10.19 And they gave, etc. THE SAME, ibid. First they cast away the unlawful wives, etc., down to make worthy of a perpetual reward in heaven.
